transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bringing you in today?

Yeah, hi, thanks. Well, honestly, I'm here because I'm just getting it from all sides right now. Mostly, people keep saying I’m not listening. And it's not like I'm trying to ignore anybody, you know? I'm really not. But my wife, for example, she'll be standing right there in the kitchen, looking right at me, talking straight to me about her day or the bills or something, and I swear I'm looking right back at her. But then a minute goes by, and she expects an answer, and I realize I only caught maybe half of it. I have to stop and ask her to say it again, which just starts a whole argument because she thinks I don't care. 

And it's not just her! It's happening at work, too. I work production, out on the floor, and my supervisor will pull me aside to go over a change on the line or a safety thing, and he's talking straight to me, and I'm nodding along, but then I get back to my station and I'm like... wait, what did he just say? I end up having to go track him down and ask him to repeat the whole thing. It’s embarrassing, being 42 years old and having your boss think you just don't respect him enough to listen. But I just... I don't know, it just doesn't stick. So that's really what brought me in today, just constantly having to ask people to repeat themselves.
Does this difficulty with focusing and retaining information happen in other situations as well, like when you're reading, watching TV, or doing something you enjoy?

Well, honestly, I don't really know about other situations. I mean, I guess I haven't really noticed it happening when I'm watching TV or doing stuff I like. But then again, I don't really read much, you know? Never really had the time or the patience for it. I'd rather be doing something with my hands, fixing something around the house, working on my truck, that kind of thing. 

But even then, when I'm working on the truck, I'm just... I'm doing it. I'm not really trying to listen to anybody or remember a whole list of instructions. It's just me and the engine. And TV, well, if I miss something on TV, it's not like the TV is going to get mad at me and start an argument, right? So maybe it happens, maybe my mind wanders off during a commercial or even in the middle of a show, but there's no consequence, so I don't really log it in my brain as a problem. It's really just the conversations—when someone is standing right there, expecting me to take in what they're saying and hold onto it. That's where I'm really feeling it, because that's when I get the look from my wife or the sigh from my boss. So as far as the other stuff... I couldn't tell you for sure. I just haven't paid attention to it like I have with people talking to me.
When you're working on your truck or doing other hands-on tasks, do you find yourself getting distracted easily or having trouble staying focused on what you're doing?

Well, see, that's the thing about working on the truck. It's not like I get distracted in the way you might think, where I just stop and walk away to do something else. It's more like... okay, so last weekend, I was out in the garage, right? And I was supposed to be changing the oil on the Chevy. I had the pan out, I had the wrench, I was ready to go. But then I looked at the wrench and realized it was covered in grease from the last time I used it. So I go over to my workbench to get a rag to wipe it down. But while I'm at the workbench, I see this box of spark plugs I bought like three months ago and never put in. 

And I think to myself, "Man, I really need to get those spark plugs in." So I start opening the box of spark plugs. But to do that, I have to move this pile of mail that I brought out there for some reason—probably to sort through it away from the noise in the house, you know how it is. Anyway, I move the mail, and underneath the mail is that missing socket I was looking for two weeks ago! I was so mad when I lost that socket. So I pick up the socket, and I'm looking at it, and I'm thinking about how I need to put it back in the set so I don't lose it again. 

So I walk over to the tool chest to put the socket away, and I realize the whole drawer is a mess. It's just a disaster in there, wrenches and ratchets all jumbled up. And I can't stand a messy tool drawer, so I start organizing the drawer. I'm taking everything out, lining it all up by size, wiping down the drawer liner... and before I know it, two hours have gone by. My wife comes out to the garage and asks if I'm done with the oil change yet, and I'm standing there with a handful of wrenches, the oil pan is still sitting under the truck completely empty, and I haven't even touched the drain plug. 

So, I don't know if that's getting distracted or what. I mean, I was doing stuff the whole time! I wasn't just sitting around twiddling my thumbs. I was busy, I was focused on the tools, I was organizing... but I guess I wasn't focused on the oil change, which was the whole point of being out there in the first place. It's like I start one thing, and that leads to another thing, and that leads to another thing, and suddenly I'm miles away from where I started. And it's frustrating, you know? Because I really did want to get that oil changed. But it's just like my brain takes these detours, and I don't even realize I'm on a detour until someone points it out to me. So, yeah, I guess you could say I have trouble staying on track, even with the hands-on stuff. It just looks a little different than when I'm trying to listen to somebody talk.
Do you find yourself losing track of time or getting off-task when you’re doing other routine activities, like grocery shopping, getting ready in the morning, or following through on personal goals?

Well, to be honest with you, doc, I don't really know about all that. Like, grocery shopping? My wife handles all of that. She learned a long time ago that if she sends me to the store, it's just a hassle. I don't even like going, to be honest. The fluorescent lights, the people just standing there blocking the aisles with their carts, looking at fifty different kinds of mustard... it just rubs me the wrong way. So she just does it. She has her whole system, she goes on Sunday mornings before the church crowd gets out, and she gets it done. So I couldn't really tell you if I lose track of time there, because I avoid the grocery store like the plague. 

And getting ready in the morning? Man, I've been working the exact same shift at the plant for, what, fifteen years now? My feet hit the floor at 4:30 AM on the dot. I don't even have to think about it. It's pure muscle memory at this point. I stumble into the bathroom, brush my teeth, throw on my jeans and my steel-toes, grab the thermos my wife sets out for me on the counter, and I'm out the door. I don't even turn the big overhead lights on half the time because I don't want to wake anybody up. It's just boom, boom, boom, out the door. There's really no room to get off task because I'm barely even awake, you know? I just do the exact same motions every single day. So I definitely haven't noticed any missing time or anything like that in the mornings. 

And as for, you know, personal goals? I'm not really sure what you mean by that. Like, New Year's resolutions or something? I don't really do those. I'm a simple guy. I just want to put in my hours, get my paycheck, keep the lights on, and maybe have a couple of beers on the back porch on a Friday night. I don't have some big five-year plan written out on a whiteboard or anything like that. I just take things one day at a time. 

So... yeah, I guess the short answer is I don't know, or at least, I haven't noticed it. It really just seems to be the conversations with my wife and my boss, and that weird stuff in the garage. The rest of my routine is just... well, it's just my routine. I don't really stop to analyze it.
Do you ever find it really hard to get started on tasks, even ones you know you need to do, like paying bills or starting a project at work?

Well, no, not really. I mean, take the bills, for example. Like I was saying about the grocery shopping, my wife pretty much handles all the paperwork for the house. She’s got this little roll-top desk in the corner of the living room, and she’s got her calculator and her little filing system with the colored tabs... she’s real organized like that. She sits down on the 15th and the 30th of every month and just knocks it all out. If it were up to me, honestly, I’d probably just rip the envelope open the second I pulled it out of the mailbox, write the check right there standing on the porch, and stick it back in the box just to get it out of my hands. I don't like things just sitting around waiting to be done. 

And as for work, you know, starting a project... Doc, I work on a production line at the plant. We don’t really have "projects" the way you office folks do. I’m not sitting at a desk staring at a blank computer screen trying to figure out how to type up a report or whatever. When the morning whistle blows, the line starts moving, and you just go. The parts come down the conveyor, you do your job, you pass it down. You don’t have to find the motivation to start, because the work is literally coming right at you at twenty feet a minute. You just keep up. 

But even with stuff around the house, like chores or fixing things, I definitely don't have a hard time getting started. If anything, it’s the exact opposite. If I see something that needs doing, I just jump right into it. Like, if I'm walking up the driveway and I see the gutters are overflowing with leaves, I don't go inside and sit on the couch for three hours dreading it. I don't even think about it. Next thing I know, I'm already halfway up the aluminum ladder in my good work boots before I even realize I should probably go grab some leather gloves so I don't cut my hands up. 

That’s kind of how I ended up with that whole mess in the garage I was telling you about. I don’t have a problem starting things at all. I start a million things! I just dive right in, head first, usually without even making a plan. It's just... you know, finishing them, or sticking to the one thing I actually went out there to do, that's where things get a little muddy. But getting the ball rolling? Nah, I've never had an issue with that. I'm usually moving before I even know what I'm doing.
Do you often feel restless, like you need to be moving or doing something all the time, even when you're trying to relax or sit still?

Well, yeah. Oh, man, yeah, absolutely. That’s actually a huge point of contention with my wife, to be honest with you. Because, you know, she wants to have that normal downtime. Like, say it’s a Friday night, right? I’ve put in my forty hours at the plant, we’ve had dinner, and she just wants to sit on the couch and watch one of those two-hour crime mystery shows she likes. A normal guy would just sink into the cushions and relax. But me? I can't do it. I just can't. 

If I have to just sit still there, staring at the screen... it’s not just that I get bored, it’s like this actual physical thing. When I have to sit still, it feels like pressure building up inside my chest and legs. It gets so intense, like I’ve got to move or do something right now or I’ll crawl out of my skin. 

So I’ll start bouncing my knee. Just tapping my foot, shaking the whole couch. And she’ll give me that look, you know, the side-eye, and she'll sigh. So I try to stop. I’ll grip the armrests and just force my legs to stay still. But then all I can think about is how much I need to move, and that pressure just gets worse and worse. So after about ten minutes, I’m up. I’ll tell her I’m just getting a glass of water. But then I'm in the kitchen, and I notice the trash is getting full, so I take that out. And while I'm outside, I see the porch light is flickering, so I go to the garage to find a bulb... and you know how that goes, based on what I told you earlier. 

And she’s calling out from the living room, "Can’t you just sit down and relax for five minutes?" And the thing is, Doc, I want to! I really do want to just sit there with her. But sitting still is... it's honestly torture. It's like I have a motor running inside me that just doesn't have an off switch. Even if we go out to eat, or if I'm sitting in the pew at church on Sunday, I’m constantly shifting my weight, looking around, folding the church bulletin into tiny little squares, stretching my neck out... I just can't do the relaxing thing. If I'm not doing something with my hands or on my feet, that pressure just takes over completely.
